# GitHub diff oracle for the diff-engine evaluation, version 1

[RFC-BPR-0082](../../../../docs/rfcs/RFC-BPR-0082-diff-engine-evaluation.md)
compares each candidate's hunks with GitHub's. This fixture holds GitHub's
hunk headers for the evaluation corpus, recorded on 2026-10-13 from the
owner's designated live test repository `MikeMarcin/BPR-Test`.

`oracle.json` lists, per corpus comparison, the base and head blob identities
and GitHub's `@@ -a,b +c,d @@` numbers. **No patch text is kept**, so no
corpus content (including the GPL-2.0 Git sources the corpus borrows) is
committed here. The corpus itself is regenerated by
`tests/evaluation/diff_engine/scripts/prepare_corpus.py`, which attaches a
recorded entry only when both regenerated blob identities match it.

## How it was recorded

`tests/evaluation/diff_engine/scripts/record_oracle.py --execute` pushed one
base branch (every left side) and eighteen group branches (the right sides of
a few files each) and opened one pull request per group, numbers 52 to 69,
each closed after it was read. A first single pull request, number 51, passed
GitHub's per-pull-request diff budget: after about 160,000 changed lines the
file list reported `+0 -0` and no patch, so the corpus was split.

For each group the script read the REST file list and the raw `.diff`. The
file list omits the patch of a large file; the raw diff still has it. The two
differ in one rule: the file list joins two hunks that one unchanged line
separates, as `git diff --inter-hunk-context=1` does, and the raw diff does
not. On all 58 files that had both, joining the raw diff's hunks that way
gave exactly the file list's hunks, so `hunks` is the file list's patch where
it exists and the joined raw diff otherwise (`hunk_source`). `hunks_raw` keeps
the raw diff's own headers.

Every live call was a read except the branch pushes, the pull-request creation
and closing. `X-RateLimit-Remaining` stayed above 4,880.
